expected_refusals.detail: comparison d16fe4449194774a8ca629c3c34597de was already classified resolved_by_stage by event 0000000000000000000000000000000a — one classification per comparison, because the edge id carries the kind and a second verdict would open a second edge rather than amend the first
comparison d16fe4449194774a8ca629c3c34597de classified resolved_by_stage, which RESOLVED the pair apart — opening an edge over it is the crying-wolf failure this whole pipeline exists to prevent
comparison 00000000000000000000000000000000 was never detected or registered — a classification of a pair nobody put forward is a verdict with no case
the classification's endpoints are not the tuple comparison 2822c2c578c15128199506ec0d7c56a9 was minted from — side for side, because both bodies order left as the canonically-first endpoint

outcome same_meaning is a semantic judgement and arrives only through an applied classify_conflict proposal — a deterministic rule claiming it would put a model's job in the reducer with none of the review

outcome resolved_by_stage is a typed comparison over recorded qualifiers and is deterministic only — a model that could decide it could resolve a real conflict away by being confident about arithmetic

edge a51b3fd02a735bd0c3705441ef296aa9 was already opened by event 00000000000000000000000000000012 — exact replay is deduplicated at the door by `contradiction-open:<store>:<edge>`, so a second event reaching the reducer is a duplicate append
addressed_by_event_id 00000000000000000000000000000002 is not a member of this batch — a close travels with the mutation that addressed the edge, and there is no standalone close path

batch member 1: edge a51b3fd02a735bd0c3705441ef296aa9 was already closed by event 00000000000000000000000000000017 — a closed edge never reopens, and a second close would be a second answer to a question that has one
member 1 refused — whole batch has no effect
relation 1b9e254efbfb3f4bbb89be2e72fe7b64 is a Supersedes, not a contradicts — registering a comparison from it would put a conflict in the ledger that nobody declared

comparison 9e5cedc292af444b2de2630bafd24ccd already exists (event 0000000000000000000000000000001f) — registration is the one creation, and an exact retry is deduplicated at the door by its idempotency key
a checkpoint through 0000000000000000000000000000001d is already recorded (event 00000000000000000000000000000021) — the same coverage claimed twice
the backfill saw 9 relations and accounts for 4 — every relation it read is either resolved apart or has an open edge, and a marker that does not add up is a marker that stopped early
this checkpoint saw 2 relations and the previous one saw 4 — the backfill reads a growing prefix, so a shrinking count is a run that lost its place
